To find the rank of $H,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}H & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $2$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $2$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\text{rank}(H)=2.$
